========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, I suppose I'm here because... frankly, because no one else seems to be paying attention to what's actually going on, and I just need someone to look at the facts. For months now—really, it's been going on since at least the late spring, maybe even earlier if I look back at my notes—I’ve been seeing this exact same pattern. 

You see, I supervise an administrative office, I have a degree in this, so I know exactly how scheduling and billing systems are supposed to run. I know what a normal error looks like. But suddenly, my sister’s appointments? They just get moved. Out of nowhere. I'll have it confirmed on the calendar, and then I find out it was rescheduled and absolutely no one told me. And the bills! The bills show up wrong, routed to the wrong place, or the amounts are completely off, which never used to happen. 

And when I call to follow up—which I always do, because I keep meticulous records of all this—these people supposedly just "forget" to call me back. I mean, it's one thing if a receptionist misses a message once, we're all human, but this is constant. It's every single time. And everyone around me, my family, the office staff, they just wave their hands and say, "Oh, it’s just clerical mistakes, people are just so busy these days." 

But I know better. I see what's really happening. It's not mistakes. They are intentionally keeping information from me. It's all completely orchestrated to push me out of the loop and push me out of making decisions regarding my sister. I mean, you don't just have this many "accidents" happen to one person unless there is a clear agenda, you know? It’s just so obvious to me that they want me out of the picture, and I've been documenting all of it because I need someone to see what they're doing.

Harm me physically? No, I don't think they're going to, you know, attack me in the street or anything like that. But actively working against me? Oh, absolutely. Without a shadow of a doubt.

But I know exactly what they are doing. I've run an office for over two decades, I know the difference between a simple filing error and a coordinated freeze-out. I know they’re keeping information from me on purpose. It’s not incompetence, it’s interference. They are actively trying to push me out of the loop and push me out of making any decisions regarding my sister's care. They want me entirely out of the picture so I can't oversee what they're doing, and frankly, it's exhausting having to fight this hard just to stay informed when it's my own sister. Well... yes and no. I mean, of course, I’ve *considered* it. I’m a rational person. Like I said, I supervise an administrative office myself. I’ve been doing it for over twenty years. I know what an oversight looks like. I know what happens when someone hits the wrong key on a keyboard or when a new hire files a chart under the wrong letter. I’ve trained dozens of people, so believe me, I am intimately familiar with human error. 

But you have to look at the sheer volume of it. If it were just one appointment getting moved, or just one bill going to the wrong address, or just one phone call slipping through the cracks... fine. I could accept that. I would have accepted that back in May, or maybe June. But it’s not just one thing. It’s a constant, unrelenting pattern. 

I actually have it all tabbed in my binder—the blue tabs are for the scheduling "errors," the yellow tabs are for the billing "mistakes," and the red tabs, well, those are the unreturned phone calls. And when you look at it all laid out like that, chronologically, the statistical probability of all these things happening to the exact same person, regarding the exact same patient, month after month... it’s just not possible. It defies logic. 

And that’s what frustrates me so much about my family. They just want to take the easy way out and say, "Oh, they’re just busy." But they aren't the ones tracking it. They aren't the ones calling the clinic at 9:00 AM on a Tuesday, waiting on hold for twenty-two minutes, leaving a detailed message with someone named Sarah, and then never hearing back. I am. 

So, yes, I’ve considered that they might be mistakes. But I’ve ruled it out. The evidence just doesn't support it. I know what I’m seeing, and I know they are deliberately keeping information from me. They want to push me out of the decision-making process for my sister, and they’re using this facade of administrative incompetence to do it. It’s the perfect cover, really, because who questions clerical errors these days? But I do. Because I know better.

I'll have it confirmed on the calendar, and then I find out it was rescheduled and absolutely no one told me. And the bills! The bills show up wrong, routed to the wrong place, or the amounts are completely off, which never used to happen. \n\nAnd when I call to follow up—which I always do, because I keep meticulous records of all this—these people supposedly just \"forget\" to call me back. I mean, it's one thing if a receptionist misses a message once, we're all human, but this is constant. It's every single time. And everyone around me, my family, the office staff, they just wave their hands and say, \"Oh, it’s just clerical mistakes, people are just so busy these days.\" \n\nBut I know better. I see what's really happening. It's not mistakes. They are intentionally keeping information from me. It's all completely orchestrated to push me out of the loop and push me out of making decisions regarding my sister. I mean, you don't just have this many \"accidents\" happen to one person unless there is a clear agenda, you know? It’s just so obvious to me that they want me out of the picture, and I've been documenting all of it because I need someone to see what they're doing.\n\nDoctor: Do you think anyone is actively working against you or trying to harm you in this situation?\n\nPatient: Harm me physically? No, I don't think they're going to, you know, attack me in the street or anything like that. But actively working against me? Oh, absolutely. Without a shadow of a doubt. \n\nLike I was just saying, this isn't just a one-off thing, it's a deliberate campaign. For months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern play out, week after week, and it's impossible to ignore if you're actually paying attention. I'll have my sister’s appointments perfectly scheduled, written down in ink on my planner, and then suddenly they get moved and I'm the only one who isn't notified. The bills show up completely wrong, routed to some old address or with these bizarre charges that make no sense. And the staff... I leave perfectly clear, professional voicemails, and they supposedly just \"forget\" to call me back. Over and over again. \n\nIt’s infuriating, really. And what truly gets under my skin is that everyone else—my family, the people at the clinic—they all just brush it off. They look at me like I'm overreacting and say, \"Oh, it’s just mistakes, they're short-staffed, the system is just so overwhelmed right now, don't take it personally.\" \n\nBut I know exactly what they are doing. I've run an office for over two decades, I know the difference between a simple filing error and a coordinated freeze-out. I know they’re keeping information from me on purpose. It’s not incompetence, it’s interference. They are actively trying to push me out of the loop and push me out of making any decisions regarding my sister's care. They want me entirely out of the picture so I can't oversee what they're doing, and frankly, it's exhausting having to fight this hard just to stay informed when it's my own sister. I actually brought my binder with me today, I have all the dates and times highlighted if you want to see exactly how they've been doing it...\n\nDoctor: Have you considered the possibility that these events could be due to mistakes or oversights rather than a deliberate campaign against you?\n\nPatient: Well... yes and no. I mean, of course, I’ve *considered* it. I’m a rational person. Like I said, I supervise an administrative office myself. I’ve been doing it for over twenty years. I know what an oversight looks like. I know what happens when someone hits the wrong key on a keyboard or when a new hire files a chart under the wrong letter. I’ve trained dozens of people, so believe me, I am intimately familiar with human error. \n\nBut you have to look at the sheer volume of it. If it were just one appointment getting moved, or just one bill going to the wrong address, or just one phone call slipping through the cracks... fine. I could accept that. I would have accepted that back in May, or maybe June. But it’s not just one thing. It’s a constant, unrelenting pattern. \n\nI actually have it all tabbed in my binder—the blue tabs are for the scheduling \"errors,\" the yellow tabs are for the billing \"mistakes,\" and the red tabs, well, those are the unreturned phone calls. It defies logic. \n\nAnd that’s what frustrates me so much about my family. They just want to take the easy way out and say, \"Oh, they’re just busy.\" But they aren't the ones tracking it. They aren't the ones calling the clinic at 9:00 AM on a Tuesday, waiting on hold for twenty-two minutes, leaving a detailed message with someone named Sarah, and then never hearing back. I am. \n\nSo, yes, I’ve considered that they might be mistakes. But I’ve ruled it out. The evidence just doesn't support it. I know what I’m seeing, and I know they are deliberately keeping information from me. They want to push me out of the decision-making process for my sister, and they’re using this facade of administrative incompetence to do it. It’s the perfect cover, really, because who questions clerical errors these days? But I do. Because I know better.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's any possibility that your interpretation of these events might be incorrect?\n\nPatient: Incorrect? Honestly, Doctor... no. I really, truly don't. And I know how that sounds, believe me, I do. I know that when someone sits in a chair like this and says they are absolutely certain of something, people tend to raise an eyebrow. My own brother did that just last Sunday at dinner! But you have to understand my position here. \n\nI am here today, talking to you, precisely because for months now—since at least April, maybe even late March if we look at the very first instance in my binder—I have been seeing this exact same pattern. It is undeniably consistent. I mean, think about it... my sister's appointments get moved without a single notification to me, the primary contact. The bills show up completely wrong, with these baffling routing errors that just happen to delay my access to them. And the staff... they just conveniently \"forget\" to call me back. Every. Single. Time. \n\nAnd even when everyone around me, from my family to the clinic manager, says it’s just mistakes, that I'm just reading too much into normal administrative hiccups... I know they are keeping information from me. I know it in my bones, and I know it from my data. They are trying to push me out of the decisions regarding my sister's care. \n\nIf I were incorrect, the errors would be random, wouldn't they? A missed call here, a wrong address there, affecting different people, different patients. But they aren't random. They are entirely focused on cutting me out. It's a concerted effort. So no, I don't think my interpretation is incorrect. I think I'm the only one actually looking at the reality of the situation, and I just won't let them get away with it.\n\n[Instruction]\n- Give candidates as ICD-10 codes, not disease names.\n- If the list changed from the previous candidates, say in \"note\" what this turn added or ruled out. It’s my sister’s appointments getting moved without my consent, the bills showing up completely wrong, the staff miraculously \"forgetting\" to call me back... it is all directed at me. I know they are keeping information from me. \n\nThey are specifically targeting me because I am the one who holds them accountable. A special role? A mission? Well, I wouldn't use words like "mission," Doctor. That makes it sound like I'm some sort of crusader in a cape, or... or someone who watches too many spy movies. Conspiracies? Please, Doctor, let’s not use words like that. It makes it sound like I’m looking for aliens in the backyard or wearing a tin foil hat. I am a rational, educated woman. Even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know the truth. I know they are deliberately keeping information from me. Even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know the truth. I know they are deliberately keeping information from me. They are doing everything in their power to push me out of the decisions regarding my sister's care because they know I am the only one actually watching them. \n\nSo no, I am not seeing \"conspiracies\" in random things. I am seeing a very specific, very real pattern of behavior directed at me, and quite frankly, if you would just look at the green section of my binder—the section where I've cross-referenced the phone logs with the billing dates—you would see exactly what I mean. Doctor, with all due respect, I supervise an entire administrative department. I handle end-of-month reconciliation, vendor disputes, and personnel scheduling for a very busy office. Doctor, I... are we going in circles? Because I feel like you are asking me the exact same question you just asked, just using slightly different words. 

No. Never. I have never had thoughts like this before. 

If you are trying to find some sort of lifelong pattern where I just imagine people are out to get me, you are going to be very disappointed. If a vendor at work sends the wrong supplies, I don't think they're "working against me." I think someone in their shipping department misread a SKU number. I pick up the phone, I clarify the error, and we fix it. That is how my brain works. I assume competence until proven otherwise.

It takes an overwhelming amount of evidence for me to finally conclude that someone is intentionally sabotaging me. An absolute mountain of evidence. Which is exactly why you have to understand how serious this situation is with my sister's care team. I didn't just wake up one morning and decide they were working against me because of one lost message. It took months of them ignoring my calls, months of them changing her appointment times without notifying me, months of them refusing to provide the itemized statements I am legally entitled to see as her care coordinator. 

So, no. To answer your question again, I have never had these thoughts before. Because before these past eleven months, I had never encountered a group of people so maliciously determined to block me from doing what needs to be done. I am only having these thoughts now because it is the only logical conclusion to the facts I have gathered in that binder.
